title: Robust gap recovery and crediting for interrupted streaming sessions
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description:
Problem: Live streaming sessions (HTTP chunked / WebSocket / SSE) sometimes get interrupted by transient network drops, client resume attempts, or server-side handoffs. When interruption occurs we currently either: 1) risk double-crediting when fragments are retransmitted, 2) under-credit when finalization never arrives, or 3) attribute credits to the wrong logical session when IDs are recycled. This ticket scopes a robust gap recovery and crediting strategy that minimizes both customer-visible billing noise and internal accounting divergence across components (gateway, metering service, ledger).

Goals: define deterministic reconciliation rules for interrupted/paused streams, implement checkpointing and gap-detection hooks, and add a background reconciliation job that heals ambiguous or orphaned credits. Ensure end-to-end telemetry and e2e tests covering out-of-order resumes, duplicate fragments, partial finalizations, and multi-tenant proxies.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming sessions expose a monotonic session sequence token (session_seq) and fragment offset that the gateway emits on every chunk
Metering service consumes fragments and emits provisional ledger entries marked 'pending' until a canonical finalization arrives or a deterministic timeout/heuristic completes finalization
Resume attempts reuse session_seq and fragment offset; duplicates are detected and deduplicated deterministically with no double-charge in >99.99% of simulated interruptions
Background reconciliation job can identify orphaned 'pending' credits older than threshold and either finalize or rollback with audit trail
Dashboard shows per-session reconciliation status and a new alert when orphaned-credit ratio exceeds 0.01% for any customer tier

Comprehensive integration tests (simulated client, gateway, metering, ledger) validating: full resume, partial resume, overlapping fragments, client reconnect with new session id, server-side model-swap with midstream handoff
tech_design:
High-level approach:
1) Session identity and sequencing: require gateway to attach stable session_seq and per-chunk sequential offset (integer) to every ingested fragment. If unavailable, gateway returns 412 precondition when client attempts resume.
2) Provisional ledger entries: metering writes provisional entries keyed by session_seq+offset+fragment_hash. Finalization transitions provisional->committed. Provisional state prevents immediate customer-facing billing until commit rules are satisfied.
3) Duplicate detection: use fragment_hash + session_seq + offset; keep sliding-window bloom + short-lived unique index for hot sessions to dedupe quickly.
4) Time-based heuristics: if finalization not received within X (configurable, default 90s) and last fragment offset increased since provisional, mark provisional as committed to avoid underbilling. If no progress for Y (configurable, default 24h), run reconciliation job.
5) Reconciliation job: runs across ledger microshards, identifies 'pending' entries older than threshold, tries to fetch session history from gateway (via tracing store) to determine finalization; if unavailable, apply conservative rules: rollback fragments that have no matching committed successor, commit ones with drift evidence. Every action produces an audit record and a signed claim used for later chargebacks.
6) Rate-limiter interplay: provisional credits should not count toward hard quota enforcement; soft quotas use provisional view but do not cause blocking. Upon commit, counters are atomically applied; on rollback, decrement stashed provisional counters.
7) Observability: emit metrics session_reconciliations_total, orphaned_pending_ratio, dedupe_false_positive_rate, provisional_commit_latency. Add tracing spans across gateway->metering->ledger for sample sessions.
8) Backwards compatibility: introduce a toggle (feature flag per-tenant) to enable the provisional pipeline for Dedicated and Hosted; Private customers can opt-in.

Data model (flat): provisional_entry_id (string), session_seq (string), offset (int as string), fragment_hash (string), state in {pending, committed, rolled_back}, created_at, last_seen_at. All transitions append signed audit events to ledger-audit topic.

testing_plan: Unit tests for dedupe index and provisional state transitions. Integration tests in CI: simulate 100k sessions with injected network drops (parameters: drop_rate, reconnect_delay, fragment_dup_rate). Staging E2E run with real gateway and ledger using canary feature flag at 1% traffic for 48h. Define regression test that reproduces previously seen undercrediting bug and assert it no longer occurs.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature branches, run migration to add provisional partition. 2) Enable feature flag for internal test tenants, validate metrics for 24h. 3) Canary at 5% hosted traffic for 72h with alert thresholds: orphaned_pending_ratio > 0.05% OR provisional_commit_latency > 3s triggers immediate rollback. 4) Gradually expand to 50% then GA. For Dedicated/Private, coordinate manual opt-in and perform per-tenant sweep for older gateway clients.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Provisional entries increase DB write amplification and storage. Mitigation: store_light entries (compressed) and expire older pending entries with compaction job.
Risk: Deduplication false positives could drop legitimate fragments. Mitigation: conservative dedupe TTL and metrics to detect elevated false_positive_rate; rollback path exists in reconciliation.

Risk: Interaction with hard rate-limiter may allow bursts when provisional credits are not counted. Mitigation: soft-quota signals will apply provisional view; hard quotas remain enforced using committed counters only.

Risk: Customers with old clients that don't send session_seq will get 412 on resume. Mitigation: gateway fallback path to use connection-id-based heuristics for best-effort, but encourage client upgrades via SDK release notes and migration window.
Risk: Reconciliation mistakes may cause retroactive chargebacks. Mitigation: audit trail, signed claims, and a manual review queue for high-dollar corrections (> $1000).
notes: This ticket is complementary to the 'session snapshot' initiative; coordinate with infra to ensure tracing sampling includes session_seq for sampled flows. We'll follow-up with a short RFC for the provisional entry schema before main implementation merges.
